question.prompt:
Define a sequence recursively by \(x_0=5\) and

\[ x_{n+1}=\dfrac{x_n^2+5x_n+4}{x_n+6} \]

for all nonnegative integers \(n.\) Let \(m\) be the least positive integer such that

\[ x_m\le4+\dfrac{1}{2^{20}}. \]

In which of the following intervals does \(m\) lie?

solutions.title: Bound the excess above four
solutions.explanation:
Because the target is close to \(4\), track the excess above \(4\). Set \(y_n=x_n-4\). Then \(y_0=1\), and
\[
y_{n+1}
=\frac{x_n^2+5x_n+4-4(x_n+6)}{x_n+6}
=\frac{(x_n-4)(x_n+5)}{x_n+6}
=\frac{y_n(y_n+9)}{y_n+10}.
\]
For \(y_n>0\), the multiplier \(\frac{y_n+9}{y_n+10}\) is positive and less than \(1\). Therefore the sequence remains positive and decreases, so \(0<y_n\le1\). Consequently,
\[
\frac9{10}\le\frac{y_{n+1}}{y_n}
=1-\frac1{y_n+10}
\le\frac{10}{11}.
\]
Starting from \(y_0=1\) and multiplying these bounds gives
\[
\left(\frac9{10}\right)^n\le y_n\le
\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^n.
\]
We only need bounds strong enough to select an interval for \(m\).

First,
\[
\left(\frac9{10}\right)^4=\frac{6561}{10000}>\frac12,
\]
so
\[
y_{80}\ge\left(\frac9{10}\right)^{80}
=\left[\left(\frac9{10}\right)^4\right]^{20}
>\frac1{2^{20}}.
\]
Since \(y_n\) decreases, the threshold cannot be reached by index \(80\). Thus \(m>80\).

For an upper bound, the binomial expansion has positive terms beyond its first two, so
\[
\left(\frac{11}{10}\right)^{10}
=\left(1+\frac1{10}\right)^{10}
>1+10\cdot\frac1{10}=2.
\]
Taking reciprocals gives \(\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^{10}<\frac12\). Therefore
\[
y_{200}\le\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^{200}
=\left[\left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^{10}\right]^{20}
<\frac1{2^{20}}.
\]
Thus \(m\le200\). We have proved \(81\le m\le200\), which lies within \(\boxed{[81,242]}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
